# donor-v0.3.21 — PTX rebuilt at ISA 8.0: the CUDA path comes back on r570 hosts (and with it the card's REAL VRAM)

**What it fixes:** `kernels.ptx` was generated by a CUDA **13.0** toolchain, which stamps `.version 9.0`. A driver can only JIT PTX at or below its **own** ISA version, so every host on r570 / CUDA 12.8 failed `cuModuleLoadData` with `CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION` and fell back to wgpu. Observed live on a rented RTX 4090 (driver 570.172.08):

```
[cuda] PTX MODULE LOAD FAILED (cuModuleLoadData) on device 0 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090' (cc 8.9):
       DriverError(CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION, "the provided PTX was compiled with an unsupported toolchain.")
[multi] GPU slot 0 → wgpu/vulkan (2047 MB binding cap)
[donor] backends: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 [wgpu]
```

**Why it cost more than throughput.** The per-binding capacity advertised to the brain comes from the **active** backend — `compute.rs:842`: *"Per-engine per-binding cap in MB (CUDA → VRAM, wgpu → adapter limit)"*, and `cuda.rs:196`: *"CUDA has no 2 GB cap, so this is the card's [VRAM]"*. Vulkan's `maxStorageBufferRange` is a hard 2 GB on NVIDIA, so a wgpu fallback registers **2047 MB instead of 24576 MB**. The brain's capability gate sizes the community pool off the *minimum* donor, so one fallen-back card dragged `communityComputeMB` to 2047 against an 11810 MB running floor — below the floor, with the 2.9 GB intra matrix unplaceable on a 2047 MB binding. A silent ISA mismatch presented as a capacity failure.

**The fix:** `kernels.ptx` regenerated with a CUDA **12.0** toolkit → `.version 8.0`, `.target sm_75` (unchanged). ISA 8.0 loads on every driver from **r525** up, so this stops being host-roulette. Source-only change — no kernel edits, no protocol change, no server change.

**Equivalence verified before install** (not assumed):
- identical kernel set — all 8 entries (`lif`, `spike_count`, `synapse_propagate`, `plasticity`, `fill_zero_u32`, `fill_zero_f32`, `scatter_ones_u32`, `scatter_vals_f32`)
- identical `.param` type sequence (102 params, same order)
- identical `ld` / `st` / `atom` / `bra` counts (112 / 18 / 1 / 45)
- whole-file opcode multiset identical except `mov.f32` 7→6 — 12.0's optimizer places one redundant hoisted zero-init differently across basic blocks
- `synapse_propagate` accumulator invariant re-checked explicitly in both builds: zero-init **precedes** the accumulate, then stores (old init@44 accum@73 store@172 · new init@44 accum@72 store@171)
- no ISA-9.0-only opcodes present

**Regenerating (the toolkit version is load-bearing — see the header of `cuda_kernels.cu`):**
```
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/donor-app/src:/src" nvidia/cuda:12.0.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 \
  nvcc --ptx -arch=compute_75 -o /src/kernels.ptx /src/cuda_kernels.cu
```
Do **not** regenerate with CUDA 13.x — it silently reintroduces this bug on every sub-r580 host.

**Verify on deploy:** the donor log must show `[donor] backends: <card> [cuda]` (not `[wgpu]`) and register with the card's real VRAM as the binding cap — a 4090 should read ~24564 MB, not 2047 MB. Brain side: `minDonorMB` / `communityComputeMB` reflect real VRAM instead of the 2 GB Vulkan ceiling.

**Not fixed here (separate, still open):** `main.rs:49` calls `gpu::enumerate()` unconditionally and `main.rs:88` hard-exits when it is empty, so a host with a working CUDA device but no Vulkan stack still cannot donate — `wgpu::Backends::PRIMARY` is Vulkan-only on Linux. Headless server donors therefore still need a Vulkan loader + GLVND present just to pass the gate. Tracked as RUNPOD.6.

**Build:** `cargo check --release` clean on all three feature sets — default (gui+cuda), `--no-default-features --features cuda`, and `--no-default-features`. No kernel changes, no protocol changes.
